sources.title: Information Geometry
sources.inspection: Printed pages 84, 85, and 87 visually inspected and compared with local OCR. The dual-flat definition requires torsion and curvature to vanish, affine coordinates and potentials are local, and the statistical embedding and affine embedding questions are distinct.
sources.role: Primary clarification of the historical definition and scope

sources.title: The Bonnet theorem for statistical manifolds
sources.inspection: Introduction and Sections 2.1-2.4, including Theorem 2.2 and its potential-extension proof, read from the full PDF text. Statistical submanifolds use metric restriction and orthogonal projection of the two connections. The equivalence proved there is local.
sources.role: Statistical definitions and credited local predecessor; not a global existence input

sources.title: Differentiable Manifolds
sources.inspection: Printed p.654 Theorem 1 and p.665 Lemma 19, footnote 32, and normal-neighborhood introduction visually inspected. Theorem 1 explicitly includes infinite differentiability; footnote 32 supplies the no-finite-limit-point form of the embedding.
sources.role: Smooth proper embedding dependency; the smooth tubular-neighborhood theorem and smooth bundle metrics are also explicitly declared standard inputs
